verdicts.reason: Both have the same failures. The 'See the List' CTA is pushed up against the top edge and sits on top of the headline, so it reads before the message. Headline, body and brand line are stacked tightly with no spacing, and the book cover hangs in the lower middle with dead space on both sides. A's CTA is a few pixels closer to the top edge than B's, but otherwise the two are the same.

A is a real side-by-side rearrangement: a big book cover on the left and copy on the right, which suits the format. But the CTA is small and wedged into the top-right corner above the headline, which breaks the reading order. The copy block is also tight, and the brand line is as prominent as the body text. B is just the portrait layout shrunk into a small centred column. The body text and brand line become nearly unreadable, and both sides of the canvas are wasted, so it was not adapted to the new shape.
